parties: HEG Limited (Demerged Company/Transferee), HEG Graphite Limited (Resulting Company), Bhilwara Energy Limited (Transferor Company)
headline: HEG Limited receives NCLT sanction for Composite Scheme of Arrangement involving demerger and merger
sum: NCLT Indore has sanctioned a composite scheme of arrangement among HEG Limited, newly created HEG Graphite Limited and Bhilwara Energy Limited, involving a demerger and merger of business undertakings. The order was notified to NSE on 18 August 2026.
implication: Composite scheme under Sections 230–232 CA 2013 involving a multi-step demerger (HEG → HEG Graphite) combined with a merger (Bhilwara Energy) represents a complex capital restructuring; watch for implementation mechanics (share swaps, effective dates, regulatory conditions precedent on stock exchange approvals and minority discent petitions).
detail: The National Company Law Tribunal, Indore Bench, has passed an order sanctioning a composite scheme of arrangement (Scheme) amongst three parties: HEG Limited (the transferee and demerged company), HEG Graphite Limited (a newly created resulting company), and Bhilwara Energy Limited (the transferor company), along with their respective shareholders and creditors. The scheme is structured under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and related provisions. The company disclosed the order to the National Stock Exchange on 18 August 2026.

framework.note: Central; permits schemes of arrangement and reconstruction subject to NCLT sanction; core statutory gateway for this demerger-cum-merger structure.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 391–394 (erstwhile compromise regime; now superseded by 230–232)
framework.note: Statutory transition; courts/NCLT now apply Ch. XI (230–232) for all schemes post-2014 reforms.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 – Regulation 37 (Material Related-Party Transactions)
framework.note: If HEG–Bhilwara or HEG–HEG Graphite involve related-party dealings, RPT disclosures and approvals will be required.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 – Regulation 37(1A) & Schedule (Substantial Acquisition; Change in Control)
framework.note: Post-scheme share structure may trigger disclosure under regulation 29 (Acquisitions/Change of Control) if shareholding shifts >5%.

framework.ref: NCLT Rules, 2016 – Rule 8 & 9 (Court Meetings; Sanction Order)
framework.note: Governs NCLT procedure for scheme approval, shareholder/creditor voting thresholds, and sanction criteria; Indore Bench applied these rules.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 391(6) & 394(1) (Alternative Dispute Resolution; Takeover Code implications)
framework.note: Demerger may trigger takeover code provisions if post-scheme shareholding results in acquisition of control; review SEBI ICDR Reg 2018 Part II-C.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 – Section 2(19AA), 47 & Schedule IV (Demerger Definition; Exemption Conditions)
framework.note: For tax-neutral treatment, scheme must satisfy statutory demerger criteria; applies to transfer of undertaking under Section 47.

framework.ref: Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code, 2016 – Section 238 (Cross-Border Insolvency; Stakeholder Protections)
framework.note: Not directly triggered here; but if any transferor company (Bhilwara Energy) in resolution, moratorium/distribution waterfall may apply.

conditions: Shareholder approval at convened court meeting(s) – thresholds per NCLT Rules 2016
Creditor meeting(s) and creditor approval if scheme affects creditors
Stock exchange approvals (NSE/BSE) for listing of resulting company shares (HEG Graphite Limited) and any share allotments
approvals: NCLT Indore Bench – scheme sanctioned (18 Aug 2026)
Shareholder meeting(s) – court convened per Sections 230–231 CA 2013
Creditor meeting(s) – if scheme impacts creditor rights
NSE intimation filed 18 Aug 2026; pending stock exchange final approval for listing of resulting company
structure.novel: Composite scheme (demerger + merger in one structure) involving three parties (HEG Limited as transferee, HEG Graphite Limited as newly created resulting company, Bhilwara Energy Limited as transferor) under unified NCLT sanction; multi-leg statutory reconstruction rare in Indian practice outside pure mergers.

triggers.note: Scheme of arrangement & reconstruction; NCLT sanction mandatory before implementation.
Court meeting procedure; shareholder & creditor voting; sanction order mechanics.
Disclosure & approval of material transactions; change in control/substantial acquisition post-scheme.
Tax-neutral demerger treatment conditional on statutory compliance.
